79th Independence Day Celebrated at MGIMS
Saturday, 16 August 2025
1609 Hits
The Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences, Sevagram, celebrated the 79th Independence Day with pride and enthusiasm on its campus. The event was graced by the presence of Shri P. L. Tapadiya (President, Kasturba Health Society), Dr. B. S. Garg (Secretary, Kasturba Health Society), Dr AK Shukla (Dean, MGIMS), Dr. Poonam Shivkumar Verma (Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital), Dr. Ramesh Pandey (Deputy Medical Superintendent, Kasturba Hospital), and other esteemed dignitaries.
The tricolour was unfurled by Mr. Adarsh Bansal, Final MBBS Part II Topper (Batch 2020), symbolizing the values of academic excellence and youthful leadership. As the flag soared high, the gathering of students, faculty, staff, and employees joined in saluting the nation with reverence.
The programme began with the
Jhanda Geet
presented by students of Kasturba Vidya Mandir, followed by patriotic songs rendered by students of Kasturba Nursing School, Kasturba Nursing College, and MGIMS. The atmosphere brimmed with devotion to the motherland, as music and voices blended to express the spirit of unity.
Addressing the gathering, the Chief Guest, Shri P. L. Tapadiya, emphasized the deeper meaning of independence.
“Independence is not just about political freedom but about empowering every individual with health and education. Sevagram holds a special place in India’s journey to freedom, reminding us of Gandhiji’s vision of self-reliance and service. Today, as a nation, we must address the ‘missing middle’—those who often fall through the cracks of our healthcare systems. True freedom will be realized only when no one is left behind.”
The programme concluded with the National Anthem, sung in unison, instilling a renewed sense of pride and responsibility. The celebration witnessed active participation from MGIMS, Kasturba Nursing College, Kasturba Nursing School, and Kasturba Vidya Mandir, making the occasion memorable and meaningful. In response to the Prime Minister’s
Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam
campaign, students, faculty, and staff also participated in a tree plantation drive at the hostels premises.
